I have a pure, burning hatred for Brawlhalla—and somehow, I love it more than ever.

This game has a special talent for turning one match into a full emotional journey. One second, I’m landing a perfect combo and feeling unstoppable; the next, I’m flying off the stage because I missed one attack by a pixel. Every loss feels personal, every opponent suddenly looks like a professional, and every time I say, “Okay, last match,” I somehow end up playing five more.

But that’s the magic of it. Brawlhalla is fast, chaotic, and ridiculously satisfying when everything clicks. Pulling off a clean read or making an impossible comeback feels amazing—and just when I’ve decided the game is the worst thing ever made, it gives me one of those moments that reminds me why I keep coming back.

So yes, I hate Brawlhalla. I hate how frustrating it can be, how it makes me blame the game instead of my own decisions, and how it keeps tempting me into “one more match.” But I love the competition, the chaos, and the feeling of finally getting it right.

In short: Brawlhalla is the game I love to hate—and the game I hate to stop loving. 

If you want to jump off a cliff but have a good time doing so then play this game.
